messages:
Maria Chen: Thinking out loud — instead of whole-model precision profiles, can we try per-operator granularity for the migration? Might reduce quality regressions while keeping perf wins.
Kevin Patel: per-operator? curious about perf overhead. router/runtime has to look up more keys per op, right?
Maria Chen: yeah small lookup overhead. proposal: profiles contain operator-level hints (preferred_quant, fallback_chain). runtime caches decisions per-shard to avoid per-token cost.
Sophie Lee: sounds promising for quality. How do we evaluate regressions though? per-operator changes could have subtle downstream effects.
Maria Chen: plan: shadow sampling + differential eval. capture outputs from canary traffic under new per-op profile and compare against baseline with targeted eval prompts.
Kevin Patel: runtime concerns: memory for operator map, and the header size in request if we carry explicit overrides. prefer compact keys: e.g. "oq:fp8,int8,4bit" per op id rather than big JSON.
Maria Chen: agreed. Draft DSL for profiles (very compact):
```
# profile proto (sketch)
model: gptx-7b
operators: [
  { id: conv1, prefer: fp8, fallback: [int8,4bit] },
  { id: mha_kv, prefer: int8, fallback: [fp8,4bit] },
]
meta: { calibration_version: "2026-03-15" }
```
Sophie Lee: love the fallback chains. We should gate automatic fallback to only degrade within a measured quality budget. put a per-op max-deg-percent in profile.
Kevin Patel: telemetry explosion risk if we emit per-op metrics for all traffic. propose sampling 1% detailed op-level telemetry + aggregated counters for everyone.
Maria Chen: yep: sample 1% full op traces; emit per-op counters (requests, fallbacks, avg_latency_ms) every minute.
Sophie Lee: rollout strategy?
Maria Chen: step 0: internal canary via shadow sampling (0.5% live traffic) + offline evals. step 1: 5% canary (apply per-operator profile with telemetry sampling). step 2: 25% with auto-fallback enabled. step 3: 100% if no quality regressions. each step gated by regression thresholds and SLOs.
Kevin Patel: sounds fine. need runtime feature flags for: profile-lookup-mode (model/global/per-operator), fallback-enforcement (auto/manual), telemetry-sample-rate.
Sophie Lee: add a lint that flags profiles where fallback chain is strictly worse on eval corpus. block deploy if it fails.
Maria Chen: ops-bot: create ticket template for per-operator profile rollouts?
ops-bot: Created task ML-4287: "Per-operator quant profile rollout checklist" assigned to Maria Chen, Kevin Patel, Sophie Lee. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-4287 :white_check_mark:
Kevin Patel: action items: 1) runtime: cheap op-id cache + compact header support (KP). 2) runtime: telemetry sampling + aggregated counters (KP). 3) ML: build differential eval harness and per-op lint (Maria). 4) Product/QA: construct canary prompts and quality thresholds (Sophie).
Sophie Lee: timeline?
Maria Chen: aiming for internal shadow by next week (7 days), 5% canary in 3 weeks if all green.
Kevin Patel: noted. I'll prototype the compact header today: format suggestion: op header string like "op:conv1=oq:fp8|int8,op:mha_kv=oq:int8|fp8" to keep parsing linear.
Sophie Lee: include config to force-disable operator-level for sensitive endpoints (PII/LLM-safety)
Maria Chen: good call. Also add a short-term perf guard: if avg extra-latency per-request > 2ms then revert to model-level profile automatically.
Kevin Patel: ok. I’ll add that auto-revert check to the runtime canary controller.
Maria Chen: ok thanks — will update ML-4287 with eval plan and sample prompts.
Sophie Lee: thanks all :thumbsup
